subparts.final_answer: $\text{The } y\text{-intercept is } 0, \text{ and the } x\text{-intercept is } 0.$
subparts.solution:
When $x = 0$, $y = -1 + 2^{-0} = -1 + 1 = 0$
$\therefore$ the $y$-intercept is $0$, and the $x$-intercept is $0$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The $y$-intercept is found by evaluating $y$ when $x=0$. Since the origin $(0,0)$ is a point on the graph, the $x$-intercept is also $0$.
step_by_step: Since the point $(0,0)$ lies on the curve, the graph passes through the origin.

subparts.stem: Find any asymptotes of the function.
State the domain and range of the function.
subparts.solution:
The domain is $\{x \mid x \in \mathbb{R}\}$.
The range is $\{y \mid y > -1\}$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Exponential functions of the form $a^x$ are defined for all real numbers and strictly positive, so $2^{-x} > 0$ for all $x$.
step_by_step: Domain: $2^{-x}$ is defined for every real $x$, so $\{x \mid x \in \mathbb{R}\}$.
Range: Since $2^{-x} > 0$ for all $x$, adding $-1$ yields $y = -1 + 2^{-x} > -1$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Writing $y \ge -1$ instead of the strict inequality $y > -1$.

subparts.final_answer: $Graph of $y = -1 + 2^{-x}$ showing passing through the origin $(0,0)$, horizontal asymptote $y = -1$, and decreasing exponential curve.$
subparts.solution: Graph showing decreasing exponential curve $y = -1 + 2^{-x}$ passing through $(0,0)$ and approaching horizontal asymptote $y = -1$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Sketch a reflection of $2^x$ in the $y$-axis shifted downwards by 1 unit.
step_by_step: Draw the dashed horizontal line $y = -1$ as the asymptote.
Mark the intercept at the origin $(0,0)$.
Draw the curve decreasing from top-left, passing through $(0,0)$, and approaching $y = -1$ from above as $x \to \infty$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Drawing an increasing exponential graph instead of a decreasing one.
